All right, I've just finished a full playtest run after cleaning up the temporary debug scripts and tweaking the emissive factor in the renderer. The playtest reported “86/86 checks passed,” which is a great sign that the functional aspects of the game are solid. However, the core issue we were chasing is visual: the black box that appeared in the ultra graphics preset at 1280×720 resolution. I made several changes to the renderer to clamp values, guard against NaNs, and reduce the emissive intensity, and I verified those changes by re‑running the ultra‑preset debug script (dbg‑caps2.mjs). The script executed without errors, but I haven't yet inspected the resulting screenshot (dbg‑ultra.png) to confirm the black box is gone. 

Rather than manually opening the image, the repository includes a visual‑audit script (visual‑audit.mjs) that programmatically captures screenshots for all relevant presets and resolutions, then prints a concise summary line at the end (e.g., “audit complete: 0 failures”). Running this script will give me a definitive, automated confirmation that the rendering fixes have eliminated the black box across the board. 

I need to execute the visual audit and capture its final output line, which contains the summary status. The Bash tool is perfect for this: I can invoke `node visual-audit.mjs`, pipe both stdout and stderr (`2>&1`) to ensure I catch any errors, and then pipe the result to `tail -1` to grab just the last line. This mirrors the pattern I've used earlier (e.g., grepping playtest output) and keeps the output concise for the user. 

I'll issue a Bash command with a descriptive label so the user knows this is the final visual verification step. The command will be:

`node visual-audit.mjs 2>&1 | tail -1`

I'll set a generous timeout (10 minutes) just in case the audit takes a while on this environment. This should give us the final visual audit result, confirming whether the black box issue is truly resolved.
